bull_bear.body:
- Designing capabilities that create and sustain market differentiation
- State-of-the-art and integrated manufacturing, printing, and converting capabilities
- An engaged and experienced team
- First-mover advantage in glue-less films - the Company was the first in India to establish glue-less film manufacturing capability, introducing an adhesive-free product to the domestic market, now witnessing strong and growing acceptance
- Over four decades (since 1981) of setting standards on high quality and innovation, and a major role in developing India's flexible packaging industry
- Well-established and recognised manufacturer of surface protection films, positioning it to benefit from rising demand in the category
- Products well accepted in international markets and competing effectively with global players, with the 'China+1' sourcing theme providing headroom
- Post-merger consolidation of all group business and operating entities under Ecoplast Limited, broadening the portfolio across surface protection films, specialty films and PE bags
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- US export tariffs and trade-policy uncertainty — Management lists Export Tariffs as a threat: with the USA a key export market, additional tariffs on Indian products pose a meaningful risk to export realizations and order flow. This already bit in FY26 - increased trade tariffs announced by the USA on India, and the resulting uncertainty, affected export orders and realizations during the year, forcing the Company to develop new customers in other export markets.
- Commodity / raw material price and availability volatility — The principal raw material is a variety of plastic polymers that are derivatives of crude oil, sourced primarily from the US, Middle East and Europe, with domestic prices generally in sync with international prices. Volatility in crude oil prices, rupee movement and the world demand-supply scenario affect the effective price and availability of polymers. In the last quarter of FY26 the escalation of the conflict in West Asia significantly affected raw material availability and pricing, impacting both margins and demand.
- Foreign exchange exposure skewed to imports — The Company operates internationally with a portion of business transacted in several currencies, and is exposed to FX risk through overseas sales and purchases from overseas suppliers. Management explicitly states that exports of the Company are significantly lower in comparison to its imports, so a depreciating rupee is a net cost headwind rather than a natural hedge; the exchange rate has changed substantially in recent years and may fluctuate substantially in future.
- Single-segment and single-country operating concentration — The Company's sole business segment is Plastic Films and all activities are incidental to this sole business segment, and it services both its domestic and export markets from India only - so there is no segment or manufacturing-geography diversification to absorb a shock to films demand, Indian input costs or India-specific trade measures.
- Rising domestic competition in surface protection films — Listed by management as a threat: a small number of domestic players have entered the surface protection films market, gradually increasing competitive intensity in what the Company describes as its core market.
- End-demand dependence on the infrastructure and realty cycle — Management states that demand for plastic in industrial applications, especially aluminium composite panel and surface protection film, will largely depend upon the revival of infrastructure projects as well as the realty sector, where consumption is large - making the Company's core volumes a derivative of a capex cycle it does not control.
- Merger integration and restated comparatives following the Kunal Plastics amalgamation — The auditor issued an Emphasis of Matter drawing attention to Note 40 on the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation of Kunal Plastics Private Limited into the Company from the retrospective appointed date of 1 April 2025 (NCLT order 14 May 2026, effective 28 May 2026), with the merger given effect as if it had occurred from the beginning of the preceding period per Appendix C to Ind AS 103. Opinion not modified, but FY26 and FY25 figures are on a merged basis, so reported history is not comparable to previously published standalone numbers, and the benefits of the enlarged entity are still to be delivered.
- Customer credit risk — Named in the MD&A Risks and Concerns as the risk of financial loss if a customer or counter-party fails to meet contractual obligations; exposure is influenced mainly by the individual characteristics of each customer and the default risk of the customer's industry, managed through credit approvals, credit limits and continuous monitoring of creditworthiness.

business.body: Founded in 1981, Ecoplast manufactures high-quality multilayer coextruded polyethylene and co-polymer films, having played a major role in developing India's flexible packaging industry as a supplier of lamination grade films. In view of poor margins and fierce competition in the commodity lamination business, the Company transitioned into a purely value-added product business, and since 2024 has focused on specialty films, adhesive films, surface protection films and the export market. Following the NCLT-sanctioned merger of sister concern Kunal Plastics Private Limited, one of the largest manufacturers of PE bags in India, all business and operating entities within the group now stand consolidated under Ecoplast Limited.

outlook.body:
- Exit commodity lamination films and operate only a value-added product business - since 2024 the focus has shifted to specialty films, adhesive films and surface protection films, and to the export market
- Deepen and diversify export markets in response to evolving tariff developments, concentrating on developing new customers across export markets other than the USA
- Continue developing higher value-added products to protect margins
- Complete a series of greenfield and brownfield expansions (more than Rs 75 crores committed since 2024) to lift combined annual capacity from ~9000 MTPA to ~13600 MTPA
- Consolidate all group business and operating entities under Ecoplast Limited via the NCLT-sanctioned amalgamation of sister concern Kunal Plastics Private Limited, broadening the portfolio into PE bags
- Secure raw material supply chains to ensure uninterrupted production and delivery amid global supply-chain uncertainty, while proactively monitoring raw material availability and pricing
- Manage polymer price volatility by widening the sourcing base, using appropriate contracts and commitments, and well-planned procurement and inventory strategy
- Wind up / close the economically unviable wholly owned subsidiary Synergy Films Private Limited, subject to regulatory approvals
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Since 2024 the Company has committed more than Rs 75 crores towards a series of greenfield and brownfield expansions, described as significantly reinforcing its manufacturing capabilities for the years ahead. The combined annual production capacity will go up from ~9000 MTPA (2024) to ~13600 MTPA after full expansion is commissioned. The final tranche of machinery is currently being installed and is on track for commissioning by the end of the second quarter of FY 2026-27. Together with the completion of the amalgamation of sister concern Kunal Plastics Private Limited (one of the largest manufacturers of PE bags in India) - approved by the Board on December 14, 2024, sanctioned by the NCLT on May 14, 2026 with an appointed date of April 1, 2025 and effective from May 28, 2026 - this expanded capacity places the Company on a meaningfully broadened product portfolio spanning surface protection films, specialty films and PE bags, with benefits expected to start flowing through progressively over the course of FY 2026-27. Separately, the wholly owned subsidiary Synergy Films Private Limited has been shut down since 7 December 2019 as economically unviable, and the Board approved its winding up / closure on May 22, 2024 subject to regulatory approvals.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for plastics in industrial applications, especially aluminium composite panel and surface protection film, will largely depend upon the revival of infrastructure projects and the realty sector, where consumption is large; the Government has declared various fiscal and non-fiscal packages for the revival of these sectors
- Rising demand for surface protection films, increasingly indispensable across manufacturing processes such as cutting, bending and deep-drawing and in withstanding mechanical handling during production and transportation - a trend that continues to strengthen the Company's core market
- Glue-less films, where the Company was the first in India to establish manufacturing capability, are now witnessing strong and growing acceptance, positioning the Company to capture the next phase of adoption
- Rising disposable incomes and growing awareness are driving substantial growth in personal hygiene products such as baby diapers and sanitary napkins - a structural, consumption-led trend described as a significant growth multiplier for the Company
- Substantial export headroom as products are well accepted internationally and compete effectively with global players, with the 'China+1' sourcing theme gaining momentum among global buyers
- Broadened product portfolio spanning surface protection films, specialty films and PE bags following the expansion and the Kunal Plastics merger, with benefits expected to flow through progressively over FY 2026-27
- Headwind: increased US trade tariffs on India and the resulting uncertainty affected export orders and realisations during the year, and pose a meaningful risk to export realisations and order flow
- Headwind: escalation of the West Asia conflict in the last quarter significantly affected raw material availability and pricing, impacting both margins and demand
- Headwind: resins and adhesives remain exposed to volatility in crude oil prices; a small number of domestic players entering surface protection films are gradually increasing competitive intensity
- Management states that, backed by expanded scale, broadened portfolio and disciplined execution, the Company is well positioned to sustain its growth momentum in the year ahead

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Ecoplast Limited is one of India's leading manufacturers and suppliers of premium lamination and surface protection films, producing multilayer coextruded polyethylene and co-polymer films with an annual capacity of 9600 MT.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Founded in 1981, Ecoplast manufactures high-quality multilayer coextruded polyethylene and co-polymer films, having played a major role in developing India's flexible packaging industry as a supplier of lamination grade films. In view of poor margins and fierce competition in the commodity lamination business, the Company transitioned into a purely value-added product business, and since 2024 has focused on specialty films, adhesive films, surface protection films and the export market. Following the NCLT-sanctioned merger of sister concern Kunal Plastics Private Limited, one of the largest manufacturers of PE bags in India, all business and operating entities within the group now stand consolidated under Ecoplast Limited.

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Aluminium composite panel manufacturers (linked to infrastructure and realty project activity)
- Surface protection for manufacturing processes such as cutting, bending and deep-drawing, and mechanical handling during production and transportation
- Flexible packaging industry
- Personal hygiene products (baby diapers, sanitary napkins) via MNC clients in the hygiene sector

- Exports to developing and developed countries
- United States (key export market) - hospitality industry via PE bags
- African markets - food industry via PE bags

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for plastics in industrial applications, especially aluminium composite panel and surface protection film, will largely depend upon the revival of infrastructure projects and the realty sector, where consumption is large; the Government has declared various fiscal and non-fiscal packages for the revival of these sectors
- Rising demand for surface protection films, increasingly indispensable across manufacturing processes such as cutting, bending and deep-drawing and in withstanding mechanical handling during production and transportation - a trend that continues to strengthen the Company's core market
- Glue-less films, where the Company was the first in India to establish manufacturing capability, are now witnessing strong and growing acceptance, positioning the Company to capture the next phase of adoption
- Rising disposable incomes and growing awareness are driving substantial growth in personal hygiene products such as baby diapers and sanitary napkins - a structural, consumption-led trend described as a significant growth multiplier for the Company
- Substantial export headroom as products are well accepted internationally and compete effectively with global players, with the 'China+1' sourcing theme gaining momentum among global buyers
- Broadened product portfolio spanning surface protection films, specialty films and PE bags following the expansion and the Kunal Plastics merger, with benefits expected to flow through progressively over FY 2026-27
- Headwind: increased US trade tariffs on India and the resulting uncertainty affected export orders and realisations during the year, and pose a meaningful risk to export realisations and order flow
- Headwind: escalation of the West Asia conflict in the last quarter significantly affected raw material availability and pricing, impacting both margins and demand
- Headwind: resins and adhesives remain exposed to volatility in crude oil prices; a small number of domestic players entering surface protection films are gradually increasing competitive intensity
- Management states that, backed by expanded scale, broadened portfolio and disciplined execution, the Company is well positioned to sustain its growth momentum in the year ahead

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Exit commodity lamination films and operate only a value-added product business - since 2024 the focus has shifted to specialty films, adhesive films and surface protection films, and to the export market
- Deepen and diversify export markets in response to evolving tariff developments, concentrating on developing new customers across export markets other than the USA
- Continue developing higher value-added products to protect margins
- Complete a series of greenfield and brownfield expansions (more than Rs 75 crores committed since 2024) to lift combined annual capacity from ~9000 MTPA to ~13600 MTPA
- Consolidate all group business and operating entities under Ecoplast Limited via the NCLT-sanctioned amalgamation of sister concern Kunal Plastics Private Limited, broadening the portfolio into PE bags
- Secure raw material supply chains to ensure uninterrupted production and delivery amid global supply-chain uncertainty, while proactively monitoring raw material availability and pricing
- Manage polymer price volatility by widening the sourcing base, using appropriate contracts and commitments, and well-planned procurement and inventory strategy
- Wind up / close the economically unviable wholly owned subsidiary Synergy Films Private Limited, subject to regulatory approvals

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Since 2024 the Company has committed more than Rs 75 crores towards a series of greenfield and brownfield expansions, described as significantly reinforcing its manufacturing capabilities for the years ahead. The combined annual production capacity will go up from ~9000 MTPA (2024) to ~13600 MTPA after full expansion is commissioned. The final tranche of machinery is currently being installed and is on track for commissioning by the end of the second quarter of FY 2026-27. Together with the completion of the amalgamation of sister concern Kunal Plastics Private Limited (one of the largest manufacturers of PE bags in India) - approved by the Board on December 14, 2024, sanctioned by the NCLT on May 14, 2026 with an appointed date of April 1, 2025 and effective from May 28, 2026 - this expanded capacity places the Company on a meaningfully broadened product portfolio spanning surface protection films, specialty films and PE bags, with benefits expected to start flowing through progressively over the course of FY 2026-27. Separately, the wholly owned subsidiary Synergy Films Private Limited has been shut down since 7 December 2019 as economically unviable, and the Board approved its winding up / closure on May 22, 2024 subject to regulatory approvals.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Designing capabilities that create and sustain market differentiation
- State-of-the-art and integrated manufacturing, printing, and converting capabilities
- An engaged and experienced team
- First-mover advantage in glue-less films - the Company was the first in India to establish glue-less film manufacturing capability, introducing an adhesive-free product to the domestic market, now witnessing strong and growing acceptance
- Over four decades (since 1981) of setting standards on high quality and innovation, and a major role in developing India's flexible packaging industry
- Well-established and recognised manufacturer of surface protection films, positioning it to benefit from rising demand in the category
- Products well accepted in international markets and competing effectively with global players, with the 'China+1' sourcing theme providing headroom
- Post-merger consolidation of all group business and operating entities under Ecoplast Limited, broadening the portfolio across surface protection films, specialty films and PE bags

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- US export tariffs and trade-policy uncertainty — Management lists Export Tariffs as a threat: with the USA a key export market, additional tariffs on Indian products pose a meaningful risk to export realizations and order flow. This already bit in FY26 - increased trade tariffs announced by the USA on India, and the resulting uncertainty, affected export orders and realizations during the year, forcing the Company to develop new customers in other export markets.
- Commodity / raw material price and availability volatility — The principal raw material is a variety of plastic polymers that are derivatives of crude oil, sourced primarily from the US, Middle East and Europe, with domestic prices generally in sync with international prices. Volatility in crude oil prices, rupee movement and the world demand-supply scenario affect the effective price and availability of polymers. In the last quarter of FY26 the escalation of the conflict in West Asia significantly affected raw material availability and pricing, impacting both margins and demand.
- Foreign exchange exposure skewed to imports — The Company operates internationally with a portion of business transacted in several currencies, and is exposed to FX risk through overseas sales and purchases from overseas suppliers. Management explicitly states that exports of the Company are significantly lower in comparison to its imports, so a depreciating rupee is a net cost headwind rather than a natural hedge; the exchange rate has changed substantially in recent years and may fluctuate substantially in future.
- Single-segment and single-country operating concentration — The Company's sole business segment is Plastic Films and all activities are incidental to this sole business segment, and it services both its domestic and export markets from India only - so there is no segment or manufacturing-geography diversification to absorb a shock to films demand, Indian input costs or India-specific trade measures.
- Rising domestic competition in surface protection films — Listed by management as a threat: a small number of domestic players have entered the surface protection films market, gradually increasing competitive intensity in what the Company describes as its core market.
- End-demand dependence on the infrastructure and realty cycle — Management states that demand for plastic in industrial applications, especially aluminium composite panel and surface protection film, will largely depend upon the revival of infrastructure projects as well as the realty sector, where consumption is large - making the Company's core volumes a derivative of a capex cycle it does not control.
- Merger integration and restated comparatives following the Kunal Plastics amalgamation — The auditor issued an Emphasis of Matter drawing attention to Note 40 on the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation of Kunal Plastics Private Limited into the Company from the retrospective appointed date of 1 April 2025 (NCLT order 14 May 2026, effective 28 May 2026), with the merger given effect as if it had occurred from the beginning of the preceding period per Appendix C to Ind AS 103. Opinion not modified, but FY26 and FY25 figures are on a merged basis, so reported history is not comparable to previously published standalone numbers, and the benefits of the enlarged entity are still to be delivered.
- Customer credit risk — Named in the MD&A Risks and Concerns as the risk of financial loss if a customer or counter-party fails to meet contractual obligations; exposure is influenced mainly by the individual characteristics of each customer and the default risk of the customer's industry, managed through credit approvals, credit limits and continuous monitoring of creditworthiness.
